title: Linear Transformations: A Matrix Moves the Grid
topic: Linear transformation of the plane — every 2×2 matrix bends the standard grid in exactly one way, and its two columns are the images of the basis vectors e₁ and e₂. Rotation, scaling and shear are special cases of the same machine. Closes on a hero line: a matrix is a verb.

beats.narration: What does a matrix actually do to space? Let's look.

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
A matrix moves the grid.

beats.narration: Here is the standard grid, and two unit basis vectors — e one along the x-axis, and e two along the y-axis. Every other vector is built from these two.

elements.content: Identity reference grid in chalk-300, full plane coverage, masked by radial vignette so chrome corners stay clean
x and y axes drawn through origin, chalk-200, thicker
e₁ basis vector from origin to (1,0), violet-400, labelled
e₂ basis vector from origin to (0,1), teal-400, labelled
Unit square (corners 0,0 / 1,0 / 1,1 / 0,1) filled amber-400 at low opacity
Right-panel HTML card with STANDARD BASIS eyebrow + 'e₁ along x, e₂ along y' + 'Every vector in the plane is a combination of these two'. Card has a soft dark backdrop for legibility.
elements.position: right panel, serif italic, on backdrop

beats.narration: First, rotation. Spin the whole grid by an angle theta. Watch where e one and e two land — those landing spots become the two columns of the rotation matrix.

elements.content: Identity reference grid stays in chalk-300 background
Transformed amber grid morphs identity → R(35°) over ~3.4s, holds, then returns to identity over 0.7s before next beat mounts
e₁ rotates from (1,0) to (cos35°, sin35°), violet-400
e₂ rotates from (0,1) to (-sin35°, cos35°), teal-400
Rotation matrix R(θ) with cos θ, -sin θ / sin θ, cos θ — column 1 violet, column 2 teal — on backdrop panel

beats.narration: Next, scaling. Stretch along x, squeeze along y. The basis vectors stay on their own axes, but their lengths change — and that change sits on the diagonal of the matrix.

elements.content: Identity reference grid in chalk-300
Transformed grid morphs identity → diag(1.8, 0.55), amber-400
e₁ stretches from (1,0) to (1.8, 0), violet-400
e₂ shrinks from (0,1) to (0, 0.55), teal-400
Diagonal matrix diag(1.8, 0.55) — column 1 violet, column 2 teal — on backdrop panel

beats.narration: Now shear. Hold e one in place, but slide e two sideways. Vertical lines tilt; horizontal lines stay flat.

elements.content: Identity reference grid in chalk-300
Transformed grid morphs identity → [[1, 0.8],[0, 1]], amber-400
e₁ stays at (1, 0), violet-400
e₂ slides from (0,1) to (0.8, 1), teal-400
Shear matrix [[1, 0.8],[0, 1]] — column 1 violet, column 2 teal — on backdrop panel

beats.narration: Every two by two matrix works the same way. Wherever e one lands becomes column one. Wherever e two lands becomes column two.

elements.content: Identity reference grid in chalk-300
Transformed grid morphs identity → [[1.1, 0.45],[-0.25, 1.05]] then holds (no return)
T(e₁) lands at (1.1, -0.25), violet-400, glow at end
T(e₂) lands at (0.45, 1.05), teal-400, glow at end
General matrix A with columns highlighted violet / teal + footnote 'column 1 = T(e₁) · column 2 = T(e₂)'

beats.narration: So a matrix is a verb — it does not describe space, it moves space.

elements.content: 'THE TAKEAWAY' mono eyebrow
'A matrix is a verb.' — huge serif italic, 'a verb' in amber-300
'It doesn't describe space — it moves space.' — serif italic 28px
'A = [ T(e₁) | T(e₂) ]' — small mono caption with violet / teal column labels
